root_outcome: For a selected non-terminal Task detail, Escape dismisses the open Task menu first, restores focus to its trigger, preserves the selected detail and emits no request; only a later eligible Escape closes Task detail under the existing parent exclusions.

lanes.outcome: Deliver the single nearest-layer Escape behavior through a characterized terminal guard, an observed RED, minimal menu-owned handling, and focused regression evidence.
acceptance_evidence: SC-001 and FR-001 through FR-004: the targeted route test proves non-Escape delegation, first-Escape menu-only dismissal, route and heading preservation, focus restoration, and same-event navigation suppression.

SC-002 and FR-005: the targeted route test proves focused-Title Escape preserves detail and a later eligible Escape closes detail; the existing BrainDumpOverlay Escape-owner test stays green and changed-path review proves TaskListPage exclusions are untouched.

SC-003 and FR-006: mocked-fetch call count remains unchanged from settled setup through non-Escape and first-Escape handling, and changed-path review confirms the localized frontend-only production scope.
SC-004 and terminal negative scenario: the existing terminal recovery route test explicitly asserts that a terminal task renders no Task menu.

risks: One keydown could reach both the menu and document handlers; stop propagation in the menu-owned handler and prove route stability after the first Escape.
Menu unmount could lose keyboard focus; restore the stable Task menu trigger ref and assert focus.
Over-broad interception could regress existing ownership; preserve TaskListPage unchanged and verify non-Escape, focused-field, modal-owner, terminal-task, and later eligible Escape behavior.
non_goals: Changing Task menu actions, terminal-task controls, Task lifecycle, or task persistence.
Changing Task detail routes, list-target calculation, focused-field or modal exclusions, or panel toggling.
Adding a global keyboard manager, dependency, store, API, backend, configuration, CI, feature flag, migration, deploy, or release change.
